$comment: Home · Connections lifecycle, part 1 — the two states that need no peer at all. Both render INLINE on Home (never /connect): the pairing gate and the failure branch sit inside the Connections tab under the balance hero, which is the whole reason these boards exist next to S/connect/*. The relay in this group's URI is `relay.invalid` and is never contacted — prepareJoin is memory-only (walletpair-protocol.ts:675-690) and the failure branch never gets as far as a socket.
$order: CUMULATIVE and load-bearing. 'Scan Again' opens the QR scanner, it does NOT return the panel to disconnected — once the error state is on screen the paste row is gone and nothing further can be paired in this group. connecting first, error last.

states.note: The pairing gate INSIDE Home (ConnectionsView.tsx:159-161 -> ConnectionFlowStates.tsx:28-79): 4-digit verification code, dApp identity row, Confirm/Cancel — framed by the balance hero, the tab bar and the dock. clickNth 8 is the unlabelled ArrowRight submit (ConnectionsView.tsx:193-199): measured on this screen the rendered clickable list is 13 long and IDENTICAL before and after typing, and #8 is its only entry with no text, no aria-label, exactly one svg, box 739,497,56,56 at 1280x950. The index is fragile by nature but cannot produce a WRONG board — a miss leaves the paste row on screen and `expect` fails the state. The URI is fabricated but schema-valid, so 0100 is a pure hash of the URI's own fields (computeDappPairingCode) and appears on no other screen.

Cancel returns the provider to 'disconnected' (dapp-connection.tsx:558-568 cancelFingerprint) so the paste row is back and #8 is the arrow again; 'walletpair:?ch=zz' throws inside parsePairingUri (walletpair-protocol.ts:246) and connectToWalletPair catches it into status 'error' carrying that exact message. forbid 'Retry' pins this to the WalletPair branch: the remote-inject variant of the same card renders a second Retry button (ConnectionFlowStates.tsx:118-125).
expect: pairing URI must contain all six fields exactly once

$comment: Home · Connections lifecycle, part 2 — the live session. NO driver change and NO local peer process: the wallet reaches 'connected' the moment the relay echoes ITS OWN join back — parseChannelJoined matches on joined.pubkey === wallet.pubkey (walletpair-protocol.ts:806-812) — so the dApp side never has to exist. Pointing the URI's `relay` at the public WalletPair relay is therefore sufficient. Cross-checked with a raw `ws` client: joining wss://relay.walletpair.org/v1?ch=..&pubkey=.. answers {"type":"channel_joined", ...} echoing the joiner's own fields.
$order: MUST BE THE LAST GROUP in whatever spec file it lands in, and the last group of any driver invocation that also captures Home. A successful join persists a snapshot in localStorage ('vela.walletpairSession'); the provider restores and reconnects it on the next mount (dapp-connection.tsx:988-1013), so a later /parallel group opens on the live-session card. Proved: running this group first makes home-connections-connecting fail with 'no input for {act:type,...}' — the paste row is not there. A fresh page.goto is also what puts THIS group back at 'disconnected' after part 1 left the panel in its error branch.
$requires: Network reachability of relay.walletpair.org. If it is down the state fails its post-conditions and nothing is written (driver exits non-zero) — it cannot degrade into a wrong board.

states.note: The live-session card (ConnectionsView.tsx:230-256): elevated VelaCard with the 'D' monogram, name and URL, the status dot + 'Active', the one-connection line and Disconnect, the Connections tab carrying a '1' badge, and CONNECTION ACTIVITY · 0 below. Confirm runs the real confirmJoin; the relay's channel_joined frame flips the session to phase 'connected' (walletpair-protocol.ts:814-822) and the transport emits 'connected' (walletpair-transport.ts:505-511). Measured stable for >124 s — no flicker, no self-heal, no drop. forbid 'Couldn't reconnect' + expectRe '\nactive\n' are what separate this board from S/home/connections-reconnecting, whose card is the same layout with the pill and note swapped.
